title: The 'the source's own report →' link stage/generate.py prints on every public future page is source_ref, a field captured once at NOTARIZED and never refreshed by update_registry -- for 11 of 92 OPEN GDACS futures it now names an episode GDACS itself has moved past, by as much as 32 episodes
statement: practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py line 33 defines TRACKED_FIELDS = ("severity", "window", "what", "where"); update_registry (same file, lines 194-247) only ever compares and rewrites those four fields on a REVISED event (loop at line 230). source_ref -- set once, at NOTARIZED, from the spread `**record` at line 213 -- is not among them and is never touched again for the rest of a future's life. practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py's gdacs_futures() (lines 62-98) builds source_ref from the feed feature's own `properties.url.report`, a URL that embeds GDACS's current episodeid as a query parameter (e.g. `...&episodeid=15&...`) and that GDACS itself changes every time it issues a new episode for the same event -- confirmed by reading properties.url.report across every preserved foreknown/snapshots//gdacs.json for eventid 1104081: 7 (2026-08-12), 9 (08-17), 10 (08-21), 13 (08-25), "no reportlink found" (08-28, GDACS's own placeholder for a broken link that night), 11 (08-31), 15 (09-03), 17 (09-06), 18 (09-15) -- nine different values across nine nights for the same event, while foreknown/registry.json's gdacs-fl-1104081 entry has held source_ref="https://www.gdacs.org/report.aspx?eventid=1104081&episodeid=7&eventtype=FL" (episode 7, its 2026-08-12 NOTARIZED value) through all eight of its own REVISED events since, the most recent on 2026-09-15. Scanning every OPEN GDACS-sourced future in foreknown/registry.json for at least one REVISED event finds 11 (of 92 total open GDACS futures); comparing the episodeid embedded in each one's stored source_ref against the episodeid the same eventid carries in the newest preserved snapshot (foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-17/gdacs.json) finds 10 of those 11 where the two numbers disagree: gdacs-dr-1018332 (18 vs 21), gdacs-dr-1018431 (11 vs 14), gdacs-dr-1027449 (6 vs 8), gdacs-dr-1027450 (5 vs 8), gdacs-dr-1027465 (2 vs 5), gdacs-fl-1104081 (7 vs 18), gdacs-fl-1104121 (2 vs 14), gdacs-tc-1001297 (51 vs 55), gdacs-tc-1001305 (15 vs 47), gdacs-wf-1030252 (39 vs 40). The eleventh, gdacs-fl-1104124, is the control case: its own single REVISED event (2026-09-02, severity Orange→Red and a window change) happened not to coincide with an episode-number change at GDACS, so its source_ref (episode 1) still matches today's feed by coincidence, not by any code that checks. The worst case, gdacs-tc-1001305 (Tropical Cyclone SAUDEL-26, the same future sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json already tracks for a different registry gap), has been revised six times since 2026-08-22 -- its severity, window, what and where have all been kept current -- while its public-facing source_ref link has stood still at episode 15 (2026-09-03T10:06:48+00:00, its last REVISED snapshot) for the fifteen nights since, even as GDACS itself moved the event forward by 32 further episodes. stage/generate.py lines 474-477 read exactly this field, unconditionally, to build the per-future public page: `source_ref = future.get("source_ref") or ""`, then `source_link = f' · the source’s own report →' if source_ref.startswith("http") else ""` -- the only per-future citation link this observatory publishes, and for these 11 futures it is a link to an episode of the event that is no longer the one the rest of the page describes.
method: Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py in full: confirmed TRACKED_FIELDS (line 33) excludes source_ref and that update_registry's only field-comparison loop (lines 230-234) iterates TRACKED_FIELDS exclusively, so source_ref set at NOTARIZED (line 213, `**record` spread) is never reassigned by any later REVISED branch. Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py's gdacs_futures() (lines 62-98) to confirm source_ref's construction, `str(p.get("url", {}).get("report", "") if isinstance(p.get("url"), dict) else p.get("url") or "")` (line 97), directly from the feed's own per-feature `properties.url.report`, and confirmed by inspection that this URL string embeds GDACS's own `episodeid` query parameter. For gdacs-fl-1104081, read `properties.url.report` and `properties.episodeid` from every one of its appearances across the nine preserved foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json files in which its eventid (1104081) appears with a NOTARIZED- or REVISED-triggering change (2026-08-12, 08-17, 08-21, 08-25, 08-28, 08-31, 09-03, 09-06, 09-15), confirming both fields move together and that 08-28's raw value is the literal string "no reportlink found" (GDACS's own placeholder, not this observatory's). Cross-checked against foreknown/registry.json's gdacs-fl-1104081.source_ref and .history to confirm it has held episode 7 (its 2026-08-12 NOTARIZED value) through all eight subsequent REVISED events. Then, for all 92 OPEN GDACS-sourced futures in foreknown/registry.json, counted REVISED events in history and, for the 11 with at least one, extracted the episodeid query parameter from the stored source_ref with a regex and compared it against the episodeid GDACS's own current feed reports for the same eventid in the newest preserved snapshot, foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-17/gdacs.json (built by matching on properties.eventid). Read the one exception, gdacs-fl-1104124, in full (single REVISED event, severity and window only, source_ref episode unchanged 1→1) to confirm the drift tracks GDACS's own episode-numbering behaviour rather than firing on every REVISED future unconditionally. Read stage/generate.py lines 460-489 to confirm source_ref is the only per-future field rendered as an outbound citation link on the public site and that it is rendered unconditionally whenever the stored string starts with "http", with no freshness check. Grepped docs/*.md and practice/src/practice/foreknown/*.py for any documented intent for source_ref beyond first-capture; found none. Ran python -m pip install -e ./practice, python -m pytest practice/tests, python stage/generate.py --repo-root . and python verify.py --repo-root . after writing this file; all green, no code changed.
worth_watching_because: This is not a field this observatory declined to track for lack of a decided use -- like iscurrent (obs-2026-09-15-1) and datemodified (obs-2026-08-15-1, and sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's ongoing review) before it, source_ref sat unexamined until tonight because nothing in TRACKED_FIELDS or the tests reads it back. But unlike those two, source_ref is already load-bearing on the public site: stage/generate.py prints it, unconditionally and by itself, as the one link inviting a reader to go verify a future's claims against GDACS directly ("the source’s own report →"). For 11 open, actively-revised futures that link no longer points at the episode the rest of the page is describing -- in the worst case by 32 episodes and six revisions' worth of drift on a future (gdacs-tc-1001305) this observatory already flags elsewhere (sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json) for a different registry gap on the very same future. The gap is structural, not a fluke of one record: TRACKED_FIELDS was written (docs/2026-08-08-foreknown-001-audit-und-entwurf.md) to decide what counts as a tracked change to a future's content, and a citation URL is not content in that sense -- but nothing currently distinguishes 'the citation still points at the record we're describing' from 'the citation points at whatever GDACS happened to show the first night', and the gdacs-fl-1104124 control case shows the two can coincide by chance as easily as they can diverge by 32 episodes.
left_alone: Not proposing a code fix tonight: whether source_ref should be re-read on every REVISED event (joining TRACKED_FIELDS, or a parallel always-refreshed field) or is intentionally meant to anchor a future to the episode it was first notarized against is a design choice about what the citation is *for*, not a mechanical defect with one correct fix -- the same reasoning obs-2026-09-15-1 gave for leaving gdacs_futures() unedited when it found iscurrent unread, and the same shape sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json's own falsification clause already reserves this kind of judgement call for. Proposing it instead as foreknown/proposals/sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json (status PROPOSED) so the maintainer can decide, and so future nights can watch whether the 10-future drifted count grows, shrinks, or a fix lands. Not touching sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's own review chain with this finding: that proposal's test_rule is about datemodified staleness (days since a record's own last-touched timestamp moved), a different field measuring a different question (source attention vs. citation freshness), even though both trace back to the same root cause (GDACS-only fields TRACKED_FIELDS never reads) -- see foreknown/proposals/sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json's own derived_from for the connection instead. Separately confirmed and left unchanged: gdacs-fl-1103815's datemodified, the live counter-example sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's 2026-09-08 review flagged as newly frozen, has now held the identical value 2026-09-03T13:36:40 across all twelve preserved nights from foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-06 through 2026-09-17 (the review's own watch_for), and a second, larger instance of the same review chain's 2026-08-17-named batching risk showed up in the same scan: 17 other OPEN, zero-REVISED GDACS futures that had advanced their datemodified in step with each night's own fetch time every night from at least 2026-08-19 through 2026-09-14 all froze together, within five seconds of each other (2026-09-14T20:25:15 through :23), on the night of 2026-09-15 and have stayed frozen there for three nights running -- a live near-simultaneous batch touching an unrelated 17-record group, not the fixed 2026-02-11 historical batch the 2026-08-17 review found; that review's own proposed narrowing (exclude a value shared by more than one future) would catch this one too, but redesigning the test_rule is exactly the open item that review already deferred, so this observation adds the evidence to that open thread rather than attempting the redesign itself. Also confirmed: foreknown/registry.json's gdacs-tc-1001305 still shows no second closure (still OPEN, unchanged since 2026-09-03) so sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json stays PROPOSED, not promotable, for the reason its own falsification clause already names. The GDACS feed composition streak obs-2026-09-15-1 left open (frozen seven nights, iscurrent zero-true for four) broke on 2026-09-15 as that observation's own text allowed for (7 removed / 6 added; iscurrent recovered to 1 true and has held there through 09-17) -- checked and not re-reported as a new finding since the prior observation already named both possible outcomes. memoryhole/readings/2026-09-16.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions (entries[].abstentions empty on all 83 entries), so no verdicts file is due tonight. registry-stall-check ran clean this morning (autonomy/log.jsonl, 2026-09-18T05:41:45+00:00, stale: []). darkocean's dma sub-source outage (autonomy/log.jsonl, "dma": "outage: URLError") continues for a 15th consecutive night; already covered by obs-2026-08-13-2.json and obs-2026-08-22-1.json and unchanged in shape, so not re-reported.
